thread:
kevin_sec: Heads-up: noticed a ~2k spike in TLS handshake failures from eu-west -> svc-queue around 2026-06-10T08:05Z. Errors show client cert CN=svc-queue-legacy. Might be tied to RBAC consolidation last week.

rita_sre: Paste a log sample? Also check KMS decrypt audit; we should only see rotator-sa doing decrypts during rotation windows.

kevin_sec: Log snippets from ingress: 
```
2026-06-10T08:04:57Z ingress-euw-2 svc-queue="svc-queue-01" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-queue-legacy, expected svc-queue)
2026-06-10T08:05:03Z ingress-euw-1 svc-queue="svc-queue-02" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-queue-legacy, expected svc-queue)
```

omar_infra: We ran RBAC regrouping on 2026-06-03 to move KMS key access from individual SAs to group:keystore-ops. There were a few manual hotfixes in the past; terraform state might have orphan entries.

rotator-bot: rotator: rotation job keystore-queue-euw-20260610-01 completed at 2026-06-10T03:30:00Z. Principal used: rotator-sa@infra.redwood

rita_sre: I pulled the KMS audit for keystore-queue-euw between 03:28-03:35Z:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-06-10T03:29:59Z","principal":"svc-queue-legacy@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/.../cryptoKeys/keystore-queue-euw"}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-10T03:30:01Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/.../cryptoKeys/keystore-queue-euw"}
```

tess_dev: That explains the CN mismatch. Legacy SA still had decrypt access and could mint certs during a staggered rollout. How did that principal keep access after the regroup?

omar_infra: Quick look at infra: terraform shows `google_project_iam_binding.keystore_legacy` left over from an emergency change in 2025. It wasn't removed during the consolidation. I'll remove the binding and reconcile state.

kevin_sec: Mitigation checklist proposal: 1) Remove leftover IAM binding (Omar), 2) run a canary rotation with rotator-sa, 3) run tiny ingress probe to verify CNs accepted, 4) add alert rule for any KMS Decrypt by principals outside allowed list, 5) add rotator pre-check to refuse rotation if unexpected principals can decrypt. Who volunteers for each?

rita_sre: I'll own the alert rule and probe. I'll wire it to page sec-oncall for now.

omar_infra: Removing binding now. Will also stage a terraform state remove and open PR to prevent reintroducing the orphan.

rotator-bot: rotator: starting canary rotation job keystore-queue-euw-20260610-canary using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

omar_infra: Binding removed @2026-06-10T08:16:12Z. Verified no legacy principals in IAM policy.

rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-06-10T08:18:07Z. Issued certs with CN=svc-queue.

tess_dev: Quick TLS check from eu-west probe: `openssl s_client -connect svc-queue.euw.internal:443 -tlsextdebug` shows server accepted client cert CN=svc-queue and handshake succeeds.

rita_sre: Rejects dropped back to baseline by 08:20Z. Alerting rule created: `kms.decrypt_principal != rotator-sa@infra.redwood && !member_of(principal, 'keystore-ops')` -> page sec-oncall. Also added weekly decrypt principal summary in the monitoring dashboard.

kevin_sec: Root cause = orphaned project-level IAM binding left after RBAC consolidation. Contributing factor = lack of monitoring/alerts for unexpected KMS decrypt principals.

omar_infra: Follow-ups: 1) I'll open PR to purge orphan state and add terraform guardrails; 2) propose a small infra test that verifies KMS IAM parity post-apply; 3) will add a note in runbook for rotations to check IAM first.

tess_dev: I'll draft an RFC for rotator to include an IAM sanity check and to abort rotation if mismatched principals present. Could be a toggle for emergency-mode.

kevin_sec: I'll file this as a P2 incident and include the timeline and audit excerpts. Add remediation timelines and owners. If anyone spots similar spikes in other regions, copy this checklist and ping here. :thumbsup:
